question: Cast cold eyes on your material and decide what sort of narrative it is, then name the tools you'll need to build it.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: Early in the process of launching a narrative, they cast cold eyes on their material and ask a fundamental question: "Just what sort of narrative are we talking about here, and what tools will I need to build it?"

question: Remember that a short piece lacks the running room to probe character complexity, so let it explore situation instead.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: A short piece of writing lacks the running room necessary to probe the complexities of character. So a general principle of fiction—that the novel explores character and the short story explores situation—also applies to nonfiction.

question: Focus a short narrative on the action line rather than on developing its characters.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: For that reason short nonfiction narratives focus on action.

question: Confine a short narrative to one or two scenes, budgeting about five hundred words as the minimum for each scene and its action line.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: Short narrative writers also must confine themselves to one or two scenes. As a rule of thumb, I figure about five hundred words as a minimum for creating a scene and the action line it contains.

question: Start a short narrative with immediate action, bursting out of the blocks, and let the arc end abruptly and precipitously.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: Short story narratives also have to start faster and end more abruptly, the narrative arc spiking up and falling precipitously. I urge writers to burst out of the blocks with immediate action.

question: Rough out a story draft as soon as you can, even before the narrative arc is complete, because the sooner you begin writing the sooner your brain begins processing the story.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: The sooner you begin writing, the sooner your brain will begin processing the story.

question: Don't close a narrative with direct quotes and a status update on a character, which flattens it into a standard news feature instead of a true story.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: But it closed with direct quotes from Lortie and an update on his condition, which kept the focus on the injured pianist and gave the story the flavor of a standard news feature, rather than a true narrative.

question: Include episodes that create both rising and falling tension in a narrative, not a single unbroken climb.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: I argued that good narrative includes rising and falling tension, which the Tchaikovsky episode provided.

question: Develop your opening into a full-fledged scene that captures the atmosphere of the place where the trouble first breaks.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: I urged David to develop the opening so that it functioned as a full-fledged scene that captured the atmosphere of the elegant restaurant where symphony president William Ryberg first heard that his star pianist was injured and couldn't play.

question: When the pivotal event of your story arrives, withhold its contents briefly to heighten the drama.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: When the fatal phone call arrived, I suggested, David should withhold its contents, heightening drama.

question: Choose a kicker word for a key spot that is one syllable, has a strong consonant sound, and carries tremendous emotional content.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: "Dreads" is a terrific kicker word, I said. It's one syllable, it has a strong consonant sound, and it has tremendous emotional content.

question: Let your own authority and voice come through in the telling, offering insight from your expertise that naive readers can't supply themselves.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: I urged David to let his authority and voice come through. As a storyteller, he was more than a music critic here.

question: Develop a minor figure into a continuing character who recurs to set up the climax and stress the doubt that heightens the drama.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: But in Version 4, Welch became a continuing character. We used him to set up Kasman's Monday performance, stressing the doubt that heightened the drama.

question: Resolve the ending's tension through a specific, electrifying image of a character's action rather than a general statement.

source.author: Jack Hart
source.quote: Most importantly, Welch gave added cachet to the ending, embodying action that created a electrifying image for readers, one that resolved tension with the power of specificity.
